        ### Question
        In the hepatic catabolism of glucose through glycolysis:

        ### Options
        opa. Glucokinase is inhibited allosterically with high concentrations of glucose.
opb. 2 molecules of NADH + H + and 4 molecules of ATP are consumed for each glucose that is oxidized to pyruvate.
opc. All reactions are reversible except those catalyzed by glucokinase, phosphofructokinase and pyruvate kinase.
opd. A high ATP / AMP ratio activates the formation of pyruvate.

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: Glucose enters the cell -> Glucokinase phosphorylates glucose -> Glucose-6-phosphate is formed -> Glucose-6-phosphate enters glycolysis -> 2 molecules of NADH + H + and 4 molecules of ATP are consumed for each glucose oxidized to pyruvate -> 90%
CHAIN: Glucose-6-phosphate is converted to fructose-6-phosphate -> Fructose-6-phosphate is converted to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate -> Fructose-1,6-bisphosphate is cleaved into dihydroxyacetone phosphate and glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate -> Dihydroxyacetone phosphate is converted to glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate -> 90%

CHAIN: Glucokinase is inhibited allosterically with high concentrations of glucose -> Inhibition of glucokinase prevents further phosphorylation of glucose -> Impaired glycolysis due to lack of glucose-6-phosphate formation -> Reduced ATP production -> 80%
